tasks.short: Write headlines, captions, cutlines and cover copy from an approved brief.

steps.what: Read the copy brief, source material and style guide.

loop.input: Copy brief, source pack and style guide.
loop.output: Requirements with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require references for factual requirements; flag contradictions and missing limits.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; unresolved requirements go to the proofreader.
loop.why_not_simpler: Briefs contain free-text instructions; structured briefs should bypass this loop.

steps.what: Write candidate headlines, captions and cover copy.

loop.input: Reviewed requirements, approved source material and channel limits.
loop.output: Up to three labelled copy alternatives.
loop.check: Check length, required wording and prohibited terms; attach references to factual claims.
loop.stop: One batch and one requested revision; unsatisfactory results return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Original wording needs language generation; fixed labels and boilerplate use templates instead.

steps.what: Check spelling, punctuation, length and required wording.
Resolve factual, tonal and contextual issues and select the preferred wording.
Approve wording for its intended audience and use.
Place approved wording in the publication draft.

tasks.design: A structured brief in {WORKFLOW} links approved sources in {DOCS}; bounded loops extract requirements and draft copy alternatives. Configured checks enforce mechanical rules, people select and approve wording, and an approval-triggered flow places the exact approved version into a {CMS} draft.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mechanical checks were already available, but varied briefs and original wording still required manual interpretation and drafting.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded language generation can produce useful first drafts. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting briefs, checks and approval records.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctive wording, implied claims, sensitive subjects and multilingual nuance still need editorial judgement. Draft quality depends on the source material.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when accurate wording is misleading, insensitive, dull or wrong for the audience.

ambition.what: Choose between caption alternatives at each weekly campaign review.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from first-draft writing toward selecting and improving alternatives. With explicit delegation, the proofreader can choose routine variants within a brief; the editor retains release approval.

reach.task: Prepare a caption comparison for a campaign experiment.
reach.learn: Audience hypotheses, controlled comparisons and interpreting campaign results.

evidence.claim: Templates and configured spelling checks can handle mechanical parts; generated captions still require review.
The proposed bounded drafting workflow is feasible, but the digest contains no direct copywriting outcome case.
Time allocations, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: This is short marketing copy within the supplied task, rather than ownership of the wider editorial strategy.
Drafts use approved source material, and publication remains a separate authorised action.
Mechanical checks reduce review effort but do not establish factual accuracy.
Build ranges cover a limited rollout. Consent and access include GDPR review and employee consultation where national rules require it; formal procedures may take longer.
EU GDPR and AI Act obligations apply according to the actual data and deployment.
unknowns: Languages, channels and typical copy volumes.
Whether briefs and style rules are structured and current.
Available connections and permissions for {DOCS}, {WORKFLOW} and {CMS}.
Who may approve factual claims and delegate routine wording choices.
Whether content contains personal data or confidential launch information.
research_questions: How much revision do generated alternatives need on representative briefs?
Which checks can be configured in the existing {DOCS} and {CMS}?
Does faster drafting improve usable alternatives or merely increase review volume?
new_work: Review generated alternatives and resolve unsupported claims.
Maintain source permissions, style rules and drafting instructions.
Handle failed transfers and prevent stale approvals from applying to changed copy.

tasks.short: Set page elements and verify dimensions, spacing and positioning against layout specifications.

steps.what: Read layout specifications and identify the current copy and illustrations.
Set copy and illustration positions in desktop publishing software {OTHER}.
Measure dimensions, spacing and positions using desktop publishing software {OTHER}.
Inspect the rendered proof for clipping, awkward breaks and visual imbalance.
Correct layout faults in desktop publishing software {OTHER} and export a new proof.
Approve the corrected proof against the layout specification.

tasks.design: Governed templates in desktop publishing software {OTHER} place approved copy and illustrations from {DOCS}, with configured checks for geometry and overflow. Deterministic scripts handle supported corrections and produce a new proof; the proofreader reviews visual exceptions and approves the exact rendered version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some checks already existed, but inconsistent templates, free-form specifications and manual file handling prevented reliable reuse.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing template and preflight features can cover much of the work. Small scripts and integrations are cheaper to build with AI coding; no model loop is needed for the baseline.
tasks.still_hard: Irregular layouts, font behaviour, multilingual expansion and physical print results need judgement. Tactile braille output requires specialist verification if it is part of the service.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing when a technically compliant page still reads poorly or directs attention to the wrong element.

ambition.what: Self-service preflight reports for regional campaign kits.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated measurements toward unusual layouts and template improvement. The proofreader retains layout conformance approval; broader design approval requires separate delegation.

reach.task: Prepare reusable layout templates for regional campaign kits.
reach.learn: Template constraints, typography, font handling and print production requirements.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx fills governed layout templates.
Geometry, overflow and repeatable layout constraints can often use configured preflight checks and deterministic scripts.
Template filling does not establish that visual judgement or physical proof inspection can be removed.
Time allocations, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Most work uses editable digital layouts and recurring specifications.
Existing desktop publishing software {OTHER} supports templates and useful preflight checks.
Automatic corrections are limited to explicit rules; ambiguous changes return to the proofreader.
The apparent manual character of this task overstates the need for people to measure routine geometry.
Build ranges cover one template family. Access includes font and asset permissions, GDPR review and consultation where national rules require it.
EU GDPR and AI Act obligations apply according to the actual data and deployment.
unknowns: The desktop publishing software category {OTHER}, file formats and scripting access.
How many layouts follow reusable templates.
Whether physical print checks or tactile braille proofing are required.
Who can approve template changes and regional variations.
research_questions: Which specification checks are already available through configuration?
Which defects escape preflight but appear in rendered or printed proofs?
How much correction work can use fixed rules without repeated reflow?
new_work: Maintain templates, tolerances, fonts and export settings.
Review visual exceptions and unsupported correction requests.
Check representative rendered proofs after template or rendering changes.
Maintain version links between source assets, proofs and approvals.

tasks.short: Read proofs aloud so a second checker can catch text and punctuation differences.

steps.what: Retrieve matching versions of approved copy and proof sheets.
Read proof aloud, naming punctuation and spelling unusual words and proper names.
Follow the spoken proof against approved copy and mark discrepancies.
Resolve disputed names, punctuation and intentional differences.
Record agreed corrections and send them for implementation.

tasks.design: A deterministic comparison job retrieves paired versions from {DOCS}, checks text and punctuation, and creates page-linked differences for review. This removes routine paired reading for eligible digital proofs; {WORKFLOW} records approved corrections and routes them to the desktop publisher, while specialist or unreliable inputs retain human checking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paired reading bridged paper proofs, unreliable extraction and weak version control. Digital comparison was already possible but often disconnected from the correction workflow.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable version identifiers, direct text extraction and inexpensive comparison workflows make routine checks easier to connect. A model loop is unnecessary for exact textual fidelity.
tasks.still_hard: Columns, ligatures, outlined text and scans can break extraction or reading order. Names need authoritative references, and tactile braille or physical output needs specialist checks.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a real error from an intended change and recognising when the source itself is wrong.
tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer paired reading sessions and more review of meaningful differences. No new editorial decision rights are created.

reach.task: Check terminology and proper-name consistency across a document set.
reach.learn: Terminology management, authoritative references and controlled document versions.

evidence.claim: Exact digital text comparison can replace oral comparison when source pairing and extraction are reliable.
A study documented invented phrases in speech-to-text output.
The digest provides no direct case measuring the replacement of paired proof reading.
Time allocations, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: This describes a supplementary paired-reading practice; many marketing teams already use digital comparison.
Reading and listening overlap in elapsed time; shares represent combined labour effort across both roles.
Routine proofs contain extractable digital text. Unsupported proofs fall back to the existing human process.
Only explicit layout characters are normalised; punctuation, spelling and proper-name changes remain visible.
Build ranges cover a limited digital workflow. Access includes content permissions, GDPR review and employee consultation where national rules require it.
EU GDPR and AI Act obligations apply according to the actual data and deployment.
unknowns: Whether paired reading remains common and why it is required.
The share of proofs with reliable text extraction and reading order.
Whether sources and proofs have stable version identifiers.
Requirements for paper, accessibility, tactile braille or independent checking.
Who may resolve source errors and intentional wording changes.
research_questions: Can representative proofs be compared without losing punctuation, names or reading order?
Which differences are harmless layout changes and which must always be reviewed?
Does comparison reduce combined labour without increasing missed discrepancies?
new_work: Review flagged differences and investigate incomplete extraction.
Maintain pairing rules and narrowly defined character normalisation.
Route unsupported proofs to human checking.
Verify that correction handoffs reference the approved proof version.

role.altitude: The role spends less time drafting routine variants, measuring page geometry and reading matching text aloud. More time goes to contextual accuracy, unusual layouts and disputed differences; wider editorial authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Marketing specialist: prepare caption comparisons linked to campaign learning.
Desktop publisher: develop governed templates and reusable preflight checks.
Technical writer: maintain terminology and document-version consistency.
skills_to_grow: Writing testable copy and layout requirements.
Evaluating generated wording against approved sources.
Configuring dictionaries, templates and preflight rules.
Understanding text extraction and comparison limits.
role.ambitious_version: Become a publication quality specialist who develops reusable checks and offers preflight support to regional teams, with explicitly delegated approval limits.
